name: TermsFeed
subcategory: legal documents, privacy compliance and business administration
tagline: Collect facts and generate clearly labeled policy drafts from user-supplied templates

pricing.notes: Policies are priced individually or as bundles rather than a stable monthly subscription.

tiers.name: Free Policy
tiers.limits: 6 policy-generator types; hosted page plus HTML, DOCX, plain-text, and Markdown download; live editing

tiers.name: Premium Policy
tiers.limits: One-time à-la-carte pricing: Privacy Policy base clause $82; optional clauses generally $14–$34; Terms & Conditions clauses $14–$24; Cookie Policy $14; Disclaimer $14; EULA clauses $14–$30; Refund Policy clauses $10–$24
tiers.notes: Final one-time total depends on selected clauses.

tiers.name: Privacy Consent
tiers.limits: Up to 1,000,000 plugin loads/month; unlimited pages, subdomains, and visits

pricing.freeTierCaps: 6 free policy types with hosting and 5 export/embed formats; credit link required; Privacy Consent has no free tier
pricing.billingTerms: policies are free or one-time à la carte; Privacy Consent is monthly or $100/year
pricing.hiddenCosts: Premium policy totals grow with every selected clause. Free policies require attribution. Privacy Consent has no trial; refund window is 7 days.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For TermsFeed, collect facts and generate clearly labeled policy drafts from user-supplied templates. The hard boundary is lawyer-drafted templates, jurisdiction updates, hosted consent tools, and compliance expertise, plus expert judgment, compliance, and regulated services.
coreLoopDIY: Collect facts, fill clearly labeled user-supplied policy templates, track versions and approvals, and repeatedly state that the output requires qualified review.
requirements: jurisdiction-specific templates supplied by the user or counsel
whatYouLose: lawyer-drafted templates, jurisdiction updates, hosted consent tools, and compliance expertise
moatNotes: expert judgment, compliance, and regulated services
ongoingBurden: law changes, jurisdiction, template provenance, access, signatures, filings, deadlines, evidence, retention, security, and professional liability
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for TermsFeed because the durable value is expert accountability and regulated execution; document generation alone cannot supply either. The recurring cost buys law changes, jurisdiction, template provenance, access, signatures, filings, deadlines, evidence, retention, security, and professional liability, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: docassemble
priorArt.desc: Open-source expert-system platform for guided interviews and document assembly.

alternatives.name: Shopify Policy Generator
alternatives.desc: Free generators for privacy, terms, refund, and shipping policies; respectable first drafts for ordinary stores, not compliance-by-checkbox.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Termly Basic
rejectedAlternatives.desc: One basic policy and no policy edits on the free tier is too cramped to replace a policy-generator subscription long-term.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Custom policy plan and a internal questionnaire and template tracker DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for TermsFeed in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and a versioned Markdown template engine; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: collect facts, fill clearly labeled user-supplied policy templates, track versions and approvals, and repeatedly state that the output requires qualified review.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create versioned questionnaires, reusable fact fields, conditional sections, templates, and approval states.
Show the source, jurisdiction, owner, reviewed date, and expiry date for every template.
Generate DOCX and PDF drafts with prominent draft and review-required labels.
Keep an immutable audit log of answers, template version, generation time, downloads, and approvals.
Add role-based access, retention, export, encrypted backups, and a deadline calendar.
Display legal-review warnings before generation and again before any final download.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out legal advice or guaranteed compliance.
Deliberately leave out government filings, identity verification, and registered-agent services.
Deliberately leave out automatic consent decisions or deployment without qualified review.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
